## Spectral module (line-by-line + HITRAN cross-sections, MT_CKD continuum, US-standard atmosphere)

### Comparison with observation (independent of the model tuning)

| Quantity | model | observed | source |
|---|---|---|---|
| clear-sky OLR, present day | 264.0 W m-2 | 268.1 | CERES EBAF Ed4.0 (Loeb et al. 2018, Table 5) |
| all-sky OLR, present day | 236.8 W m-2 | 240.1 | same |
| longwave cloud radiative effect | 27.9 W m-2 | 27.9 | same (**this is the tuning target**) |

A single US-standard profile is not a global mean, so differences of a few W m-2 are expected.  Without the water-vapour continuum and the 25 cm-1 line cut-off the model clear-sky OLR was 275 W m-2, 7 W m-2 too high.

### Cloud model

All-sky = (1 - 0.67) x clear + 0.67 x [grey deck at 5-6 km, optical depth 0.685].  Cover is the satellite global-mean cloud fraction; the opacity is the single tuned parameter; the deck height is an assumption (sensitivity in `docs/cloud_sensitivity.md`).

### Greenhouse-gas forcing (instantaneous, top of atmosphere, vs 1750 atmosphere)

* 2xCO2: 2.76 W m-2 clear sky, 2.01 all-sky (AR6 effective forcing 3.93, which includes stratospheric adjustment).
* Successive CO2 doublings add 2.76, 2.79 and 2.83 W m-2 (clear sky): logarithmic law from line physics.
* 1750 to 2019, all-sky estimate: CO2 1.12, CH4 0.51, N2O 0.19, all three 1.80 W m-2.

### Halocarbons (17 molecules, HITRAN cross-sections)

All-sky radiative efficiency / AR6 Table 7.SM.7: 1.02-1.31, mean 1.15 (clear sky: 1.62-1.95).  Full table: `docs/halocarbon_check.md`.  The AR6 values were not used in tuning.  The remaining excess over AR6 is plausibly due to the single-profile, uniform-vertical-distribution and one-deck cloud simplifications; stratospheric adjustment would push our values the other way, so it does not explain it.
